subject: maths
question: One pipe can fill a tank in 7 minutes, while another pipe can empty the completely filled tank in 14 minutes. If both the pipes are opened together when the tank is empty, how many minutes will it take to fill one-half of the tank?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Filling rate = 1/7, Emptying rate = −1/14

Net rate = 1/7 − 1/14 = 1/14

Time for full tank = 14 min

Half tank time = 14 ÷ 2 = 7 min

**∴ The correct answer = 7 minutes**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Filling pipe = 7 minutes

Emptying pipe = 14 minutes

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of Time Taken

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Time (min)**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 Filling
 7
 14
 2
 
 

 Emptying
 14
 −1
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Net efficiency = 2 − 1 = 1 unit/min

⇒ Time for full tank = 14 ÷ 1 = 14 minutes

⇒ Time for half tank = 14 ÷ 2 = 7 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 7 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes Concept

Inlet adds work, outlet subtracts work

Net Efficiency

Combined efficiency = sum of individual efficiencies

Shortcut Idea

If net rate is constant, half work takes half time
